text.p: "You're the low lifest man I've ever seen."
"You're speaking with a forked tongue."
"You've been exposed for your duplicity."
"You're an unscrupulous S.O.B."
"You treat me like I'm a god damn crook."
"You're trying to back stab me."
"You are a racist."
"We know that you're Satan."

Just another conference call in that wonderful world of professional boxing with promoter Don King at his dramatic, irate best. Not unusually bombastic, mind you, but fully cranked up, as he ranted against promoter Dino Duva of Main Events on Thursday.

Duva's strongest response to King was that it was all "bullshit" which drew a rebuke from King's heavyweight fighter, Oliver McCall, to watch his language. And later, a plea from the fighter: "Can't we all get along?"

King and Duva have been forced into a shotgun wedding for the promotion of the Lennox Lewis-McCall fight for the vacant World Boxing Council (WBC) title scheduled, but not at all certain to come off between the two 31-year-old fighters, on Feb 7 in Las Vegas.
The subject of the rancour, of course, is money.

King says Duva has not provided a letter of credit for the $3.75 million King says McCall is due for his equal split with Lewis of the purse for the fight. And King says his man will not fight if the money isn't forthcoming.
Duva, meanwhile, says he will provide the money only when he receives a properly-notarized letter, informing him whether to give the money to McCall or to King.
Duva, who won the right to promote the fight in a purse bid, says King sent him an improperly notarized letter that would not hold up legally.
What's more, King says, Duva has not provided $200,000 in training expenses for McCall, the former WBC heavyweight champion by way of his upset second-round knockout of Lewis in 1994.

Duva says he's not obligated to pay training expenses for King's fighter, who lost his title to Frank Bruno 16 months ago. Bruno subsequently lost it to Tyson last March, who then lost it to Evander Holyfield in November.
King says McCall, who assures everyone his third rehabilitation programme for drug and alcohol abuse is taking, needs the training expenses also to help him feed "his six babies."

McCall, arrested last month on charges of vandalism, disorderly conduct and resisting arrest after he threw a Christmas tree in a hotel lobby, says the money also would pay for bigger and taller sparring partners.
But, regardless, said McCall (28-6) in his best Muhammad Ali imitation, "I guarantee you within fo-ahh he's gonna hit the flo-ahh."

McCall, who says he's "walking in righteousness" these days, said of the advice Lewis (29-1) will receive from a new, improved corner, "You can tell him how to fight, but you can't put the fight in him."

But McCall, attempting to show his new-found stability, helped by seeing drug counsellors every day and having "people surround me 24 hours," said, "If the fight don't never happen I will not shed a tear.
"My greatest goal is not to be champion again, my goal is to enter the kingdom of heaven."
